constructions.latent_object: S(a, b) = T(a, b) + T(b, a)

hypotheses.construction_plan: For T(i, j), instantiate the binary kernel T(a,b) at (a,b)=(i,j). For T(j, i), apply the argument-permutation operator (a,b)->(b,a) to the same kernel, then instantiate at (a,b)=(i,j).
required_assumptions: T is a two-argument function or indexed object
i and j are independent index symbols
hypotheses.rationale: The two terms differ only by reversal of the argument list; a single binary kernel T evaluated on the S2 orbit of the ordered pair (i,j) is the minimal shared structure.

hypotheses.latent_object: S(a, b) = T(a, b) + T(b, a)
hypotheses.construction_plan: Define the two-index symmetrized object S(a,b)=T(a,b)+T(b,a). The full expression is the specialization S(i,j), i.e. S(a,b) with a=i and b=j.
required_assumptions: The sum over swapped argument order is well-defined
proof_obligations: T(i, j) + T(j, i) - S(i, j) = 0
hypotheses.rationale: The full expression is exactly the S2-symmetrization of T over its two argument slots, so it is structurally invariant under the swap i<->j.
